items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 12.f5 is the engine's best move (depth 16).
Before 12.f5 the engine at depth 16 rates the position between 0.9 pawn better for Black and level.
After 12.f5 the pawn attacks e6.
After 12.f5 the pawn attacks g6.
12.e5 is at least 0.6 pawn below the best move (depth 16).

hints: Look at what your four kingside pawns can take away from Black. Which square would you like to deny?
A pawn push can control two squares at once, and one of them is a square a knight would love.
Push the f-pawn from f4 to f5.
items.explain: The engine at depth 16 rates 12.f5 best. The position before it is rated slightly in Black's favour (between level and 0.9 pawn), so the move is a plan for later, not a win of material. The pawn on f5 attacks e6 and g6. 12.e5 is rated at least 0.6 pawn below.

feedback_by_move.e4e5: The engine at depth 16 rates 12.e5 at least 0.6 pawn below 12.f5.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 14.Bxd6 is the engine's best move (depth 16).
14.Rad1 is at least 0.4 pawn below the best move (depth 16).
After 14.Bxd6 cxd6 Black has four pawns on the queenside.
After 14.Bxd6 cxd6 Black has no doubled pawns.
After 14.Bxd6 cxd6 White has four pawns on the kingside.
After 14.Bxd6 cxd6 Black has three pawns on the kingside.

hints: Black's bishop on d6 is a useful piece. What happens to Black's pawns if White removes it?
Check what Black must recapture with, and what that does to the pawn count on each wing.
Take the bishop on d6 with your bishop.
items.explain: The engine at depth 16 rates 14.Bxd6 best, at least 0.4 pawn above 14.Rad1. After 14.Bxd6 cxd6 the doubled c-pawns are gone: Black now has four undoubled queenside pawns against three, so the trade repairs Black's queenside; White's four kingside pawns still face three. The engine rates the trade best anyway. The claims check the pawn counts, not why the engine prefers it.

feedback_by_move.a1d1: The engine at depth 16 rates 14.Rad1 at least 0.4 pawn below 14.Bxd6.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 16.Ne6 is the engine's best move (depth 16).
Before 16.Ne6 the engine at depth 16 rates the position at least 0.4 pawn better for White.
A knight on e6 attacks d8, c7 and g7.
After 16.Ne6 no black pawn attacks e6.
After 16.Ne6 a white pawn guards e6.
16.Rad1 is at least 0.5 pawn below the best move (depth 16).

hints: Look at the squares in front of Black's pawns. Is there a square your knight can occupy that no black pawn can challenge?
The pawn you pushed on move 12 may now be useful as support.
Move the knight from d4 to e6.
items.explain: The engine at depth 16 rates 16.Ne6 best, at least 0.5 pawn above 16.Rad1. The knight on e6 attacks the rook on d8 and the squares c7 and g7; no black pawn attacks e6 and the pawn on f5 guards it.

feedback_by_move.a1d1: The engine at depth 16 rates 16.Rad1 at least 0.5 pawn below 16.Ne6.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 23.g4, 23.h4, 23.Rd4, 23.Rd3 and 23.Rh3 are all within 0.4 pawn of the engine's best move (depth 16).
White has four pawns on the kingside.
Black has three pawns on the kingside.
Before 23.g4 the engine at depth 16 rates the position at least 1 pawn better for White.

hints: Count the pawns on the kingside for each side. Which of White's pieces can help them?
Several moves are close in value; g4 (the game move) and h4 both advance the kingside pawns.
Push a kingside pawn: g4 (the game move) and h4 are both fine.
items.explain: The engine at depth 16 rates 23.g4 (the game move), 23.h4, 23.Rd4, 23.Rd3 and 23.Rh3 within 0.4 pawn of each other, so there is no single answer here. White has four kingside pawns against three; g4 and h4 advance pawns of the group that has the numbers.

items.prompt: White to move. Find the best move.

claims.statement: 31.hxg5 is the engine's best move (depth 16).
31.Rh3 is at least 0.8 pawn below the best move (depth 16).
After 31.hxg5 hxg5 the a-file and the h-file are open.
Before 31.hxg5 the engine at depth 16 rates the position at least 2.5 pawns better for White.

hints: Black has pawns on g5 and h6 and you have one on h4. What could an exchange do to the files?
If the pawns come off, which file is left with no pawns at all, and who owns the rooks that could use it?
Capture on g5 with the h-pawn.
items.explain: The engine at depth 16 rates 31.hxg5 best, at least 0.8 pawn above 31.Rh3. After 31.hxg5 hxg5 the a-file and the h-file hold no pawns. White's rooks can use them.

feedback_by_move.g3h3: The engine at depth 16 rates 31.Rh3 at least 0.8 pawn below 31.hxg5.
